newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamist MP resigns in growing govt crisis.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamist MP resigns in growing govt crisis.

text.p: A Turkish MP resigned from the Islamist wing of the coalition on Thursday in a further blow to the crumbling government alliance, an official from his Welfare Party said.
"He resigned today," the official told Reuters when asked to comment on reports that Bursa deputy Ertugrul Yalcinbayir had resigned. He said the reason for the resignation was not clear.
The resignation left the coalition without a clear majority in the 550-seat parliament.
The government has been undermined by a string of defections prompted by a dispute over religious activism since the army called in February for a crackdown on Moslem revivalism.

Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan held four hours of talks on Thursday with a rightist powerbroker and coalition partner Tansu Ciller, whose conservative True Path Party has threatened to pull out of the coalition within a week.

True Path, a pro-Western party, said on Wednesday night it would withdraw from the government if Ciller, now the foreign minister, was not made prime minister by June 18 under a plan to deflect criticism of the alliance by the influential generals.
